source_refs.note: Topic printed 4.1.7.2 Applications of Trees (PDF 112-113, printed 109-110); the number 4.1.7.2 is repeated.

items: File systems: pre-order traversal backs up a directory before its contents.
File system deletion: post-order traversal deletes subdirectories and files before their parent directory.
Hierarchical data: organisational charts and family trees.
Decision making: decision trees choose outcomes from conditions.
Syntax parsing: compilers build trees to represent and process the structure of source code.

blocks.prompt: Why must post-order be used to delete a folder and everything in it?
blocks.explanation: A folder can be deleted only when it is empty, and post-order visits (deletes) all children before their parent.

items: Tree uses: backups (pre-order), deletion (post-order), hierarchies, decision trees, compilers.
